question: Of the world's greenhouse gas, which part is largest: planes, road vehicles, cement, steel or farm animals?
answer: Road vehicles, at about 12% of global greenhouse gas in 2016, then iron and steel at about 7%. Cement, at 3%, outweighs aviation at about 2%. Personal footprint calculators rarely show steel or cement, because nobody buys a tonne of either: they arrive hidden inside a car, a bridge or a flat.
move: The quiet industries that build the world can outweigh the ones people argue about.
source: Climate Watch data, via Our World in Data
reference: Ritchie, H. (2020) Sector by sector: where do global greenhouse gas emissions come from? Our World in Data, from Climate Watch and World Resources Institute data for 2016
ask: When I picture climate pollution, which industries never come to mind?

items.label: Aviation
items.note: About 2%; contrails add extra warming that this figure leaves out.

items.label: Cement
items.note: Heating limestone splits CO₂ out of the rock itself, before any fuel counts.

items.label: Road vehicles
items.note: Cars, lorries and buses: about 12%, the biggest slice here.

items.label: Cattle and manure
items.note: Methane from cattle's guts and manure: three times aviation.

items.label: Iron and steel
items.note: Coke strips the oxygen from iron ore and leaves as CO₂.
